chapter: Learning drums and recording on the Coast
title: The invitation to play for President Truman
summary: Presidential staff heard them at Milton's, a telegram summoned them to Washington, and the Statler held bourbon from the president.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: That's right, but the greatest deal was when we played for the president, and that was -- oh, man, that was something, boy. I thought the guys was joking. He had some of those little stenographers, photographers, all of them listening to us out at Milton's, you understand me, about six of them, man. When the president were here -- he were here on his own, he came here (inaudible). at home then,
Yeah, he was here for about -- I think he stayed a week or something like that. He brought all those guys with him. (Inaudible). So they

came out to Milton's -- not the president but they came out to Milton's and they were talking. They said, well we sure like your playing, talking about Julia Lee and myself. Julia was -- just the two of us were out there. Said I would like to have you -- how would you like to go to play for the president? And Julia and I laughed, you know, we didn't figure we going to (inaudible) play for the president. He said, (unintelligible) about a couple of weeks. And Julia and I are laughing, and I said, oh, baby. And a couple of weeks we got a telegram saying come to the Washington.
Where did you stay in Washington?
In fact I stayed there about six weeks ago.

Nice place, isn't it? So a cab met us, you know, and taken us out there, you understand what I mean? And we open the door and in my room there were a fifth of Kentucky Tavern with a letter on it, you know, saying compliments from the president, compliments from the president.
That's great, I hope you saved that letter.
Oh, that letter's at home. Yeah, and in Julia's room the same thing.
Great. The president knew it should be bourbon and not scotch, huh?
